findings.problem: status is a public String field accepting any value (e.g. "deleted", "foo", "sent"). No enum or domain type enforces valid lifecycle states.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can place a PacketWorkflow into any arbitrary status string, violating domain invariants. No compile-time or runtime guard prevents invalid states.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a sealed enum `pub enum PacketStatus { New, Validated, Sent }` and a fallible constructor `impl PacketStatus { fn from_str(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> }`.

findings.problem: is_validated is a public bool. Paired with is_sent bool and status String, the struct can represent contradictory states (e.g. status="sent" but is_validated=false, or is_validated=true and is_sent=true simultaneously with no ordering guarantee).
findings.failure_mode: Logical inconsistency between status, is_validated, and is_sent fields. A consumer checking only `is_validated` may act on an unvalidated packet; checking `is_sent` may miss that status is stale.
findings.fix: Eliminate `is_validated: bool`. Encode validation as part of a single typestate or enum (e.g. `PacketStatus::Validated` implies validated). Only keep `is_sent: bool` temporarily, then fold it into a typestate.

findings.problem: is_sent is a public bool with no ordering relationship to status or is_validated. A packet can be marked sent without being validated, and status can diverge from the boolean flags.
findings.failure_mode: Packet sent flow invariant (validate-then-send) is not enforceable. `mark_sent` mutates is_sent and status independently, allowing is_sent=true with status="new" after external mutation.
findings.fix: Replace `is_sent: bool` with a typestate enum `pub enum PacketState { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. The `Sent` variant owns `sent_at_epoch_ms`, making Option unnecessary and encoding the sent-at time as part of the type.

findings.problem: PacketWorkflow uses mutable public fields and a pass-by-value `mark_sent` function. No typestate or typed constructor prevents creation of a fully invalid struct (e.g. all defaults).
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct `PacketWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }` and pass it through the system with no domain validation.
findings.fix: Add a fallible constructor `impl PacketWorkflow { pub fn new(id: impl Into<String>) -> Result<Self, InvalidPacketError> }` with validation logic. Hide all fields behind a private impl and expose only domain-safe accessors.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is `Option<u64>` as a lifecycle field. It is None when not sent, but Option can be set to None after being set to Some, reversing time semantics.
findings.failure_mode: If field is mutable, `sent_at_epoch_ms = None` can clear the sent timestamp after the packet was already sent. Option as a lifecycle flag is a Holzman violation.
findings.fix: Move `sent_at_epoch_ms: u64` into a `PacketState::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }` variant. Non-sent states carry no timestamp. The type encodes the presence/absence invariant.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership of PacketWorkflow and mutates it in-place. While this is a pure function, it has no return type that signals success/failure (e.g. no Result).
findings.failure_mode: No error path. If validation were added later, this function would need to silently ignore it or be changed to a fallible API, violating API stability.
findings.fix: Change signature to `pub fn mark_sent(item: &PacketWorkflow) -> Result<PacketWorkflow, SendError>` with a typed error, and make the function fallible from the start.

residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The struct represents every illegal state combination at compile time (empty id, any status string, contradictory bools, reversible Option). The typestate pattern is required to make illegal states unrepresentable. Without benchmarks, performance claims are unsubstantiated. Without behavior tests, no lifecycle invariants are verified.
